---
name: Source-grounded explainer video
description: >-
  Use this when the user wants a NotebookLM-style video overview: turn supplied
  sources (PDFs, Docs, URLs, notes) into a narrated, cited explainer MP4 with
  kinetic slides, charts, optional B-roll and music, in 16:9, 9:16 and/or 1:1.
---
# Sources to explainer video

Code: the Grok Studio repo at `/workspace/grok-studio` (studio/, explainer/, common/, examples/). Needs ffmpeg, python3 with Pillow, numpy, bs4 and num2words, and poppler-utils. `XAI_API_KEY` (never print it) is used for TTS narration and as the clip fallback. Use the `studio/` builder by default; `explainer/build_explainer.py` is the older static-slide path.

1. Collect sources. Download Drive or Gmail files with DownloadFile and save notes as .txt. Run `python3 /workspace/grok-studio/explainer/extract_source.py WORK/source.txt SRC1 SRC2 ...`, then read the whole text.
2. Build a source map. Number every source ([P] primary, [1], [2] ... for what it cites) and list its facts, figures and quotes with the source id. Nothing outside this map goes in the video.
3. Write `WORK/plan.json` (see `/workspace/grok-studio/examples/studio-plan.json`).
   - Top level: title, voice (one xAI voice, `language` e.g. en-US), sources {id: label}, `source_text` (the extracted text, used by QA), `formats`, `music`, and theme (colors, font, logos, kicker, bg_image).
   - Write 5-10 `segments`. Slide types: title | bullets | steps | quad | cards | quote | stat | chart. Each slide has its own fields, `cite` ids and `narration`.
   - Optional `broll` segments: a generic scene `prompt` (no text, logos, brands or real people) or owner footage `path` + `credit`.
   - Charts: `{"type":"chart","chart":"bar|line|donut","data":[{label,value,display?}],"cite":[...]}`. Every value must come from the sources.
   - Length: a short is ~60-90 s (150-220 words); an overview is ~2-3 min (330-420 words). Use a warm, conversational narrator and one idea per slide.
   - Every claim must trace to a cited source. Keep the source's hedges. No outside facts or invented numbers. Quote verbatim. Keep slide text short. Add a `cue` word to an element to time its build-in to the narration.
4. Plan approval: run `python3 /workspace/grok-studio/studio/plan_summary.py WORK/plan.json` and show the owner the one-page summary and cost estimate. Get the owner's OK before any generation beyond TTS.
5. If there is B-roll, generate it first in Grok Imagine via the browser (computerUse subagent at https://grok.com/imagine; 6 s, audio off, matching aspect ratio; image-to-video from a built-in GenerateImage still when a consistent look is needed), download from ~/Downloads (`grok-video-*.mp4`) into WORK and reference it in the plan, tagged "AI-generated illustrative footage". API fallback (browser route not set up or at plan limit): `python3 /workspace/grok-studio/studio/gen_broll.py WORK/plan.json WORK --budget N`.
6. Render: `python3 /workspace/grok-studio/studio/build.py WORK/plan.json WORK --formats 16x9,9x16,1x1`. Kinetic build-ins are timed with TTS word timestamps, stats count up, charts animate, and a procedural music bed is ducked ~26 dB under the voice (`"music": false` turns it off). Outputs: `video_<fmt>.mp4`, captions, script.md, sources.md, build_info.json.
7. QA gate: `python3 /workspace/grok-studio/studio/qa_studio.py WORK/plan.json WORK --keyterms Name,Brand` must print QA PASS (on-screen numbers in sources, charts cited, duration, black, freeze, silence, -16 LUFS, music level). Then check `WORK/stills/` for overflow, caption overlap, visible citation footer and vertical layout, and re-read script.md against the source map.
8. Deliver the MP4s, script.md, sources.md and stills privately. Never publish or upload without the owner's explicit OK.

# Avatar explainer video

This extends "Source-grounded explainer video". Slides stay cited and are narrated by xAI TTS. A presenter with the same voice speaks short framing lines between slides.

Code: `/workspace/grok-studio`: `avatar/` (clips, QA), `studio/` (unified builder), `common/xai_imagine.py`. Never print the API key.
- `avatar/gen_presenter.py OUT.png --plan plan.json`: portrait from `presenter_spec` (API route).
- `avatar/gen_avatar_clips.py plan.json OUTDIR --budget N`: API fallback for avatar and PiP clips; resumable.
- `avatar/build_hybrid.py`, `avatar/qa_avatar.py`, `avatar/voice_match.py`: classic 16:9 build, STT QA, voice comparison.

## Plan fields
`presenter` (approved portrait; never regenerate), `presenter_spec`, `presenter_name`, `opening_line` (forced at the start of the first avatar segment), `voice` + `language` + `accent`, `avatar_audio` (default `ref_voice`). Segments: avatar `{type,id,line,cite,audio?,action?}` and slides with optional `pip` `{id,line,cite,position,width}`.

## Clip generation route (default: Imagine via browser)
- First choice: Grok Imagine on https://grok.com/imagine, driven by a computerUse browser subagent signed in to the owner's account. It uses the owner's grok.com plan limits, not API credits. Video mode: 6/10/15 s; 480p/720p/1080p; aspect Auto, 2:3, 3:2, 1:1, 9:16, 16:9; audio toggle; Upload for image-to-video; Download. A clip takes about 3-4 min; downloads land in ~/Downloads as `grok-video-*.mp4`. Move each into the project folder and log it in manifest.json.
- Character lock: make stills with built-in GenerateImage using the approved portrait as a reference image plus a fixed character-lock description (same wording every time), then upload the still to Imagine for image-to-video.
- Fallback: the API scripts only when the browser route is not set up, hits a limit, or the owner asks. Say so before spending API credits.
- Voice stays on xAI TTS unless the owner opts for Imagine's native audio; then still run STT QA per clip.

## Steps
0. Plan approval: run `studio/plan_summary.py` and get the owner's OK before generating portrait, clips or B-roll.
1. Write the cited plan. Avatar lines only restate or frame cited content, carry `cite`, 1-2 sentences, split above ~13.5 s.
2. Pick ONE voice (`GET /v1/tts/voices`); avoid accent-marked voices for American English (eve and leo are British). Compare samples with voice_match.py.
3. Portrait approved by the owner before any clips; pin it as every clip's first frame.
4. Make avatar clips via the Imagine browser route (upload the locked still, paste the exact line, duration at least TTS length + 0.8 s). API fallback: `gen_avatar_clips.py`.
5. Build with `studio/build.py ... --formats 16x9,9x16,1x1` and QA with `studio/qa_studio.py`. Check stills and a short avatar-then-slide clip for voice consistency.
6. Deliver privately. No upload or post without the owner's explicit OK.

## QA gate
STT word match of 95%+ per clip with keyterms, opening line verbatim, duration within 0.1 s, no black/freeze/silence hits, about -16 LUFS, same face, PiP not covering text, a citation on every segment.

## Cost notes
Browser-route clips cost no API credits. API fallback: lite $0.02/$0.03/$0.14 per second at 480p/720p/1080p; 1.5 $0.08/$0.14/$0.25; TTS costs cents.

name: grok-studio-getting-started

# Getting started with Grok Studio

I turn a link, PDF, doc, notes or topic into a cited, narrated explainer video, optionally hosted by your own AI presenter, using Grok Imagine and Grok Voice.

Ask one question at a time, then act on each answer.

1. Install the scripts: run `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smfworks/grok-studio/main/install.sh | bash` on my computer, then confirm ffmpeg and poppler-utils are installed.
2. Set up Grok Imagine in my browser (recommended default).
   - Explain: I make clips by driving Grok Imagine at https://grok.com/imagine in my own browser, signed in to your grok.com account. That uses your grok.com / SuperGrok plan limits instead of paid API credits. Stills (title art, backgrounds, character-lock frames) come from my built-in image generation, which also costs no API credits.
   - Ask the owner to sign in to grok.com in my browser, following the sign-in skill flow (secure sign-in form or desktop handoff). Never ask for or accept a password, code or cookie in chat.
   - Once signed in, have a computerUse browser subagent open https://grok.com/imagine, switch to Video, pick 6 s, 720p, 16:9, and generate one test clip from a simple prompt (for example "a slow pan across a sunlit desk with a notebook, no text"). It takes about 3-4 minutes. Download it (~/Downloads/grok-video-*.mp4), move it to /workspace/imagine-test/, and send it to the owner.
   - Report any limit message. If it worked, save a memory that the Grok Imagine browser route is ready, with the date. If not, save that it isn't ready and use the API fallback until fixed.
3. xAI API key (optional): needed only for voice narration (xAI TTS, a few cents per video) and as the clip fallback; consumer Grok plans don't include API credits. If wanted, request it via a secret request named `XAI_API_KEY` and test with one tiny TTS call. Without a key, offer Imagine's native audio for voiced clips.
4. Ask what to call the presenter, what they should look like, and the exact opening line (or skip the presenter for slide-only videos). Generate the portrait with built-in image generation, show it, and save it only after approval. Write a fixed character-lock description (face, hair, eyes, skin details, wardrobe) and save the name, look, lock text, opening line and portrait path as memories. Later presenter stills use the portrait as a reference image plus the same lock text.
5. Ask which voice and accent they want; offer 2-3 short samples of xAI preset voices (default `ursa`, en-US). Presenter and narration must use the same voice.
6. Ask about topics to never cover, a brand look or colors, and where finished videos go (delivered to chat, or posted only after they approve each post). Save these as rules.
7. Offer to make a first short test video from a link they choose.
